description: Amazon.com, Inc. is an American multinational technology company headquartered in Seattle, Washington, with a vast global geographic footprint. Its operations span three segments: North America, International, and Amazon Web Services (AWS). AWS operates 114 Availability Zones across 36 geographic regions worldwide, serving customers globally. The company employs approximately 1.576 million people (Q4 2025) and has a presence in numerous countries through its e-commerce, cloud computing, digital streaming, and artificial intelligence businesses. Key global initiatives include Project Kuiper (a LEO satellite network with 250+ satellites in space, targeting commercial services in Q3 2026), the Amazon Leo satellite constellation (20+ launches planned in 2026, over 30 in 2027), and Zoox autonomous vehicle operations with 350K+ riders. The company holds significant international investments including Anthropic and Rivian, and has made major acquisitions such as MGM Holdings and One Medical.

geopoliticalRisks.description: China-based sellers account for significant portions of Amazon's third-party seller services and advertising revenues, and China-based suppliers provide significant portions of components and finished goods. US tariffs on China and retaliatory Chinese tariffs create substantial uncertainty. China extended tariffs on critical chemical solvents, sanctioned US firms, and threatened to stop buying US semiconductors. Amazon's forward guidance cites tariff and trade policies as a source of substantial uncertainty.

geopoliticalRisks.riskLabel: GDPR Fine & Tax Disputes in Luxembourg
geopoliticalRisks.description: The Luxembourg National Commission for Data Protection (CNPD) imposed a €746 million fine on Amazon Europe Core S.à r.l. for alleged GDPR violations. Amazon also faces a Luxembourg tax authority dispute where the tax basis of certain intangible assets distributed from Luxembourg to the US in 2021 was denied. The European Commission's state aid decision against Amazon in Luxembourg (~€250M recovery) is under appeal.
geopoliticalRisks.filingReference: Amazon 10-K; CNPD fine July 2021; Luxembourg tax authority September 2022

geopoliticalRisks.description: The Italian Competition Authority (ICA) imposed a €1.13 billion fine on Amazon entities for alleged EU competition rule infringements related to marketplace and logistics practices in Italy. Amazon paid the fine and is appealing. Q4 2025 operating income includes a $1.1 billion charge for resolution of tax disputes associated with stores business in Italy and settlement of a lawsuit.

geopoliticalRisks.riskLabel: FTC Antitrust Lawsuit & Multiple State Actions
geopoliticalRisks.description: The FTC and multiple state Attorneys General filed a lawsuit in September 2023 alleging Amazon has monopolies in online superstores and marketplace services. Amazon faces multiple private lawsuits and actions by state Attorneys General (DC, California, Arizona) alleging price fixing, monopolization, and antitrust violations, seeking billions in damages. Open investigations exist in the US and European marketplace for sellers.

geopoliticalRisks.riskLabel: India Tax Dispute on Cloud Services
geopoliticalRisks.description: The Indian Tax Authority (ITA) determined that tax applies to cloud services fees paid to Amazon in the US. Amazon is contesting this position in Indian courts. Adverse resolution could require significant additional tax payments. India also restricts foreign ownership or control of Indian companies involved in online multi-brand retail trading, affecting Amazon's operations.

geopoliticalRisks.riskLabel: Semiconductor Supply Chain Risk via Taiwan
geopoliticalRisks.description: Amazon relies on a limited group of suppliers for semiconductor products including GPUs for AI infrastructure. Taiwan opened its first AI-chip smuggling crackdown, treating forged export paperwork for Nvidia-equipped servers as a smuggling matter. US export controls on advanced semiconductors to China and potential Taiwan Strait disruption pose risks to Amazon's AI infrastructure and hardware supply chains.
geopoliticalRisks.filingReference: Amazon 10-K; BIS export controls; Taiwan chip smuggling crackdown

geopoliticalRisks.description: Amazon's Project Nimbus contract with Israel (worth $1.2B+) has drawn significant controversy. The contract allegedly prevents Amazon from restricting Israel's use of services even if linked to human rights violations. Amazon suspended an employee who criticized the project. The contract operates under exclusive Israeli jurisdiction, which does not recognize the ICC. Israel faces genocide charges at the ICJ, creating substantial reputational and legal risk.
geopoliticalRisks.filingReference: Amazon internal documents; Israeli Ministry of Finance tender documents

geopoliticalRisks.riskLabel: EU Digital Markets Act & Competition Investigations
geopoliticalRisks.description: Amazon faces open investigations based on claims that aspects of its operations violate EU competition rules, including in the European marketplace for sellers. The EU's alignment with the US on China is not assured. The EU has enacted global minimum taxes and proposed taxes on online advertising and marketplace service revenues. The European Commission's state aid decision against Amazon in Luxembourg is under appeal.

Amazon settled with OFAC for $134,523 for apparent violations of multiple sanctions programs, processing orders for persons in Crimea, Cuba, Iran, Syria, North Korea, and Sudan. The UK broadened its Russian sanctions regime. Sanctions on Russia, China, the Middle East, and Africa continue to evolve. Amazon faces complex multi-jurisdictional sanctions compliance obligations.

Sky accused Amazon of not doing enough to prevent piracy of its sports rights via 'jailbroken' Fire Sticks. The UK launched the Office of Trade Sanctions Implementation with new civil enforcement authority. Amazon faces UK tax examinations and potential liabilities. The UK's Payment Systems Regulator is conducting market reviews affecting Amazon's payment services.

Amazon plans to expand into the Canadian market through an investment in a new solar plant in Alberta. Canada released proposed amendments bringing sanctions reporting obligations under the PCMLTFA. Amazon faces Canadian regulatory compliance risks as it expands operations.
geopoliticalRisks.filingReference: Amazon expansion announcements; Canadian sanctions amendments July 2024

geopoliticalRisks.description: Amazon's internationally-focused stores' functional currencies include the Japanese Yen. Changes in foreign currency exchange rates reduced International segment net sales by $15.0 billion in 2022 and consolidated net sales by $15.5 billion in 2022. Based on intercompany balances, a 20% adverse FX change would result in losses of $1.2 billion. Amazon is subject to tax examination in Japan.

Amazon is subject to tax examination by authorities in Germany. Nokia filed patent infringement complaints against Amazon in German courts, and a German court ruled Amazon infringed one Nokia patent. Amazon faces German competition and regulatory risks as part of its EU operations.

geopoliticalRisks.riskLabel: French Tax Examination & Digital Services Tax
geopoliticalRisks.description: Amazon is subject to tax examination by authorities in France. Non-US jurisdictions including France have proposed or enacted taxes on online advertising and marketplace service revenues, which could increase Amazon's tax burden. Amazon faces French regulatory compliance risks.

geopoliticalRisks.riskLabel: Middle East Conflict & Supply Chain Disruption
geopoliticalRisks.description: The US and Israel's war on Iran has disrupted transit through the Strait of Hormuz, increasing operating costs for Amazon's fulfillment and supply chains. Sanctions related to the Middle East, especially Iran, are expected to increase. The conflict creates risks for Amazon's international operations and energy costs.
geopoliticalRisks.filingReference: Amazon forward guidance; geopolitical risk disclosures
